channel.title: Violations Watch: Syria
channel.description: New incidents reported in Syria. Most entries are unverified leads, not findings.

item.title: Explosion in the Damascus countryside kills two, a father and child, and wounds one (Syrian state media)
item.description: Unverified lead (Medium priority). Jaramana, Rif Dimashq, Syria. Types: Killing of civilians. Alleged perpetrator: Unknown. Reported casualties: 2 killed, 1 injured. Grave violations against children: Killing and maiming. Disputed or caveats: Cause of the explosion not established; reports suggest security forces may have been the target. 1 source. Original reports and legal frameworks: https://violationswatch.org/#VW-2026-0754

item.title: Car bomb in Jaramana, Rif Dimashq: two killed, including a child, and up to two injured; no claim of responsibility
item.description: Unverified lead (High priority). Jaramana, Rif Dimashq, Syria. Types: Killing of civilians. Alleged perpetrator: Unknown; no claim of responsibility. Reported casualties: 1-2 killed, 1-2 injured. Grave violations against children: Killing and maiming. Disputed or caveats: Figures differ (1–2 killed, 1–2 injured); perpetrator unknown; some reports from party-affiliated channels. 5 sources. Original reports and legal frameworks: https://violationswatch.org/#VW-2026-0614

item.title: Israel has detained 49 Syrians since Assad's fall; families still without answers
item.description: Unverified lead (Low priority). Southern Syria (buffer zone). Types: Arbitrary detention & disappearance. Alleged perpetrator: Israel Defense Forces. Reported casualties: 0 killed. Disputed or caveats: Aggregate. 3 sources. Original reports and legal frameworks: https://violationswatch.org/#VW-2026-0444

item.title: Explosive remnants of war kill four children in Syria in less than a week
item.description: Unverified lead (High priority). Syria. Types: Killing of civilians. Alleged perpetrator: Explosive remnants of war. Reported casualties: 4 killed. Grave violations against children: Killing and maiming. 2 sources. Original reports and legal frameworks: https://violationswatch.org/#VW-2026-0414
